newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cera 1996 profit fanned by savings accounts, ABB.
newsitem.headline: Cera 1996 profit fanned by savings accounts, ABB.

text.p: Cera Bank, Belgium's sixth-largest, said on Thursday that 1996 profit mushroomed partly due to increased demand from investors for savings accounts and off-balance sheet instruments.
Cera's 1996 group net profit soared 71.2 percent to 5.8 billion Belgian francs.
Nearly half the rise was due to a 45.8 percent net profit rise to 3.72 billion francs at parent company Cera Bank.
Cera also profited handsomely from its 44.5 percent stake in Belgian insurance company ABB (Insurance of the Belgian Farmers' Union), which also reported strong earnings growth in 1996.
Cera's share in ABB profit rose to 1.225 billion francs from 500 million in 1995, chief executive officer Willy Breesch told a news conference.

He noted that Cera Bank's 1996 profit was boosted by a 22 percent rise in demand for savings accounts and by a 38.6 percent increase in demand for off-balance sheet instruments such as equity funds, bond funds and insurance bonds.
Cera Bank's own funds rose more than nine percent to 67.1 billion francs. Breesch noted it contained only few subordinated loans.
"So we still have room to expand. Own funds can easily go up because we have quite a few possibilities via subordinated loans," he said.
Breesch also noted that provisions remained steady in 1996 compared with 1995 despite a fall in depreciation on credits.
He said Cera set aside 521 million francs for the introduction of the euro and adjustment to computer networks before the year 2000 to cope with the "millennium bug".
"The total cost (for euro and computer adjustments) will be higher but we think that 521 million is fiscally acceptable," he said.
